findings.diagnosis: The prompt fails to treat verbal complexes (negation, resultatives, verb‑object compounds, auxiliaries/aspect markers) as atomic for entailment: it ranks cuts that orphan or split predicates too highly.
findings.evidence: ['cmn_hans_cn_236','cmn_hans_cn_398','cmn_hans_cn_979','cmn_hans_cn_880'] — these 4 cases all show policy cuts that split negated or tightly bound predicate/complement sequences, producing very high contradiction scores for the left fragment.

edit.text: Do not cut so that a negated verb, resultative, verb–object compound, auxiliary/aspect marker, or tightly bound predicate is left without its complements; keep predicates and their complements/aspectual markers together.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt overweights protecting multi-character names/transliterations/technical tokens and therefore shifts cuts to avoid splitting them, often creating isolated punctuation, reporting verbs, or short predicate fragments that become unentailed.
findings.evidence: ['cmn_hans_cn_438','cmn_hans_cn_111','cmn_hans_cn_947'] — these 3 cases share transliterations, named entities, or date/technical spans where preserving the token forced nearby punctuation or predicates into dangling, contradicted pieces.

edit.text: Do not preserve multi-token names if doing so would isolate punctuation, reporting verbs, or core predicates; prefer cuts that keep clause predicates and their punctuation/verbs intact even if a long name is split.
